paragraphs: R' Yonatan ben Akhmai. (In Kaftor VaFerach, chapter 23, the reading is 'ben Agmai'.) He was a disciple of R' Yohanan, at Sanhedrin 14a.

R' Yohanan was distressed over Rav Shemen bar Abba, that he was not among them so as to ordain him. R' Shimon ben Zirud and one with him, and who was that? R' Yonatan ben Akhmai — the one who was among them they ordained, and the one who was not among them they did not ordain. And according to Hyman's reading of the plain sense of the language, this refers to R' Yohanan, that he ordained one of them.

And indeed, Hyman says, this is stated explicitly in the Yerushalmi, at the end of Terumot and in Shabbat, chapter 2 [supplied פ״ר], end of halakhah 1: Rabbi Abbahu said, 'Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhmai taught me' — Rabbi Zeira said to him, 'And what was his distinction?' He said to him, 'He is a great man and expert in our Mishnah, and Rabbi Hiyya of Kfar Tehumin made him known before Rabbi, and he appointed him sage.' (Hyman says it is known that all the Nesi'im are called in the Yerushalmi by the name Rabbi, or it is an abbreviation of רב״י, R' Yohanan.)

notes.text: Kaftor VaFerach is cited for ben Agmai. The Yerushalmi chapter label פ״ר is irregular, and Hyman offers alternatives for Rabbi/RY in the ordination account.
The source has ופירשה, with פירסם in parentheses; the latter supports the rendering “made him known.”

The heading and the unsupported personal titles in p001/p002 remain R'; the two Yonatan occurrences are not assigned one title merely because their names match. Every explicit full Rav is retained, including Rav Shemen; Abba is untitled. Kaftor VaFerach is the inherited contextual expansion of בכו״פ, not a newly inspected chapter-23 witness; Akhmai and Agmai remain distinct supplied forms. Sanhedrin 14a is Hyman's supplied locator (כסנהדרין יד.); its older verification note remains historical, without a newly selected Sanhedrin scalar or title transfer this pass. Hyman's student relationship and plain-sense conclusion that Yohanan ordained one of the pair remain his claims; the present/absent contrast, plural they ordained, singular one, negative did not ordain, and genuine who-was-that question are preserved without resolving the pronouns into a new historical identity. Two whole saved Guggenheimer scalars were read with their raw hashes, selectors and actual edition metadata checked. Shabbat's selected scalar at text[0][19], within 2:1, explicitly names Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhmai, Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Hiyya of Kfar Tehumin, supporting those p003 titles only. Terumot's text[4][10], within 11:5, leaves Yonatan untitled and reads before Rav where Shabbat and Hyman read before Rabbi. The supplied end-of-Terumot locator and Shabbat chapter פ״ר, end of halakhah 1, remain in the translation; the digital locations are comparisons, not a repaired chapter numeral or printed correction history. The original proposal to replace the current note and declare that פ״ר stands for chapter two is not applied. Before Rabbi remains an explicit full title in Hyman. His known-all-Nesi'im explanation and alternative רב״י/R' Yohanan abbreviation retain their attribution and force; the latter title is not expanded from another passage. Supplied ופירשה (פירסם) and digital פירשה/פרשיה remain distinct; the parenthesis supports made him known, without importing a publishing event. Taught me, his distinction rather than a man Tuvia, great man, our Mishnah and the final he-appointed-him wording are preserved; the subjects of presentation and appointment are not turned into new identity bindings. Neither whole scalar's intervening lamp/oil law is imported into Hyman's compressed quotation. All earlier English and the three original mixed notes plus both current notes remain exact, with this one additive qualification. The p003 source hold remains.

The consulted scan of Hyman II, p. 703, prints Shabbat פ״ב, chapter 2, beside the supplied transcription’s פ״ר. The English follows the printed numeral; the Hebrew and the earlier irregular-label notes remain unchanged. The whole consulted Guggenheimer Shabbat 2:1 passage names Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhmai and reads “before Rabbi”; the Terumot 11:5 parallel leaves Yonatan untitled and reads “before Rav.” These readings are compared without identifying every namesake or adopting Hyman’s alternative explanation of Rabbi/RY. Hyman’s statement that all the Nesi’im are called Rabbi retains its force as his account. The whole Sanhedrin 14a passage preserves the present/absent ordination contrast and also gives an alternative ordering of the pair that Hyman omits. Its consulted Hebrew names Yonatan ben Akhmai, while Davidson’s English renders Yohanan in that passage; the supplied name is not silently changed. The view that Yohanan ordained one of them remains Hyman’s plain-sense inference. Kaftor VaFerach chapter 23 remains Hyman’s cited witness for Agmai: the exact passage has not been independently collated. The intervening lamp-and-oil law is not inserted into Hyman’s abbreviated quotation, and no title or identity is transferred between the passages.
